caption: The drawing depicts a detailed architectural element, likely a classical capital, presented in two views: a front elevation on the left and a side elevation on the right. The object is primarily rendered in shades of beige, brown, and light pink, with marbling effects suggesting a stone or plaster material. The capital consists of two vertical columns adorned with stylized floral motifs at the top and symmetrical leaf-like patterns running vertically along their lengths. Above the columns, there is an entablature featuring a decorative frieze with repeating geometric patterns, including diamonds and circles. The side view on the right shows the profile of the capital, highlighting the scroll-like volute and the thickness of the entablature, as well as the proportional relationships of the structure. Black ink is used for outlines, detailing, and measurements, which are marked in both views along the bottom and right sides, providing dimensions in inches. The background is plain, off-white, and there is a signature in the lower right corner.
title: Wall Bracket (Ecclesiastical)
